official_measurement_examples.name: Current 2026 decisions
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate common-land decisions were updated 6 July 2026; individual decisions are case-specific and are not blanket parcel permissions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 38 works consent
official_measurement_examples.fact: Restricted works on registered common land can require Secretary of State consent under section 38 of the Commons Act 2006; planning permission is a separate question.

official_measurement_examples.name: Deregistration route
official_measurement_examples.fact: Section 16 deregistration or exchange is a separate statutory process and can require replacement land and relevant ownership or charge-holder consents.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ownership separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Common land can be privately or publicly owned; common-land status does not identify the legal owner by itself.

official_measurement_examples.name: Access rights separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Rights to roam or recreation vary by land type; village-green rights and common-land access must not be collapsed into one universal access rule.

official_measurement_examples.name: Registration trigger events
official_measurement_examples.fact: Town and village green registration can be restricted by statutory trigger events; absence of a new registration application is not proof the land has no existing green status.

official_measurement_examples.name: Works category distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Some works may be outside section 38, exempt, consentable or more appropriately handled by deregistration/exchange; geometry alone cannot classify the legal route.

official_measurement_examples.name: Register evidence limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A common-land register entry is legal-status evidence but is not cadastral title, development capacity or planning approval.

core_rules: common-land status is not planning permission
section 38 consent is separate from planning permission
deregistration and exchange are separate from works consent
common-land status is not ownership proof
common-land access rights are not identical to village-green rights
case decisions are not universal parcel rules
trigger events affect new green registration applications
register geometry is not cadastral title geometry
consent to works does not determine development yield
planning permission does not remove common-land statutory controls
historic decision records retain case and date
no parcel common-land clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Planning Inspectorate, Defra, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. The 6 July 2026 decisions and 16 February 2026 deregistration update were retained with works-consent, deregistration, ownership and access separation; no parcel promotion.
